note: Command vocabulary for IHC OpenVisual UI automation. status: confirmed = verified live; partial = mechanism wired but a sub-flow is unverified; planned = declared, mechanism not yet wired. mechanism drives dispatch in aui.ps1. Add a command by adding one object here that reuses an existing mechanism. A row's `item`/`menuPath` should pin an AutomationId wherever one exists, NOT a label: the app's UI is Danish, and on 2026-08-08 eight rows were found broken because they pinned the English labels they were written against (node.getProperties looked for 'Properties' in a flyout offering 'Egenskaber…'). Ids are matched before labels on both menu surfaces, and are the app's own CommandRegistry row ids -- 'ctx.'-prefixed on the node flyout.
routeNote:
What a verb's transcript is EVIDENCE OF. `user` = the verb reaches its outcome through the same surface and the same event a person or their assistive technology would (a menu path, a keystroke, real pointer input, or a UIA pattern on the control that owns the value). `synthetic` = it reaches the outcome by a path no person can take -- posting a command straight to the app, or setting state without touching the control that owns it. `observe` = it performs no action at all; it reads. `unimplemented` = the row is declared but wired to nothing, so it is evidence of nothing.

WHY THIS FIELD EXISTS: a synthetic verb skips whatever the user's route would have raised, so its silence is not absence. The vendor MCP's product.insert posts the catalog command directly and never sees the product dialog; a comparison run concluded 'no dialog on insert' from it, and IHC OpenVisual was BUILT to match that -- then rebuilt the other way once the dialog was measured through the menu. One field on one row would have prevented the whole round trip. So: a `synthetic` verb can NEVER answer a question about checklist dimension 2 (which action triggers which response, and in what order), 13 (dialog functionality) or 14 (validation, errors, confirmations). Use it to ARRANGE state, never to measure it. An `observe` verb proves presentation only -- never interaction.

This driver currently has NO synthetic verb: every mutating row drives a real menu, key, pointer or control pattern. That is a property to preserve, not a coincidence -- if a shortcut verb is ever added, mark it `synthetic` here and it will be excluded from route evidence by rule instead of by memory.

commands.description: Readiness preflight: Windows OS, app running, main window usable.
Passive context snapshot: window title, toolbar visible, open modal, current selection.
Context snapshot (alias of session.status for run parity).
Cancel/close the topmost open modal dialog (Esc). Use to dismiss orphaned dialogs.

Enumerate the OPEN modal's controls into data as {dialog:{title}, controlCount, focused, controls:[{id, name, class, enabled, visible, focused, rect, text, items[], selectedIndex, toggleState}]}. `focused` names the control holding KEYBOARD FOCUS -- {id, name, class} beside the list, and a per-row flag -- which is how you tell a dialog that merely opened from one that opened AT a field. It is null when this app does not hold focus at all (another window is in front), which is NOT the same as a dialog that opened with nothing focused; focus is compared by UIA identity, never by AutomationId, since several controls may carry none. READ-ONLY: opens nothing, changes nothing, closes nothing -- open the dialog first (node.doubleClick / node.properties) and close it with dialog.cancel. `enabled` and `visible` are INDEPENDENT: visible:false = not rendered; visible:true + enabled:false = greyed. `id` is the control's AutomationId -- a XAML dialog's fields address as NameBox/NoteBox/OkButton/CancelButton, and since 2026-08-08 the CODE-BUILT message boxes (AvaloniaDialogService.ShowButtonsAsync) carry ids too: the window is "ConfirmDialog" and its choices are "ConfirmChoice0", "ConfirmChoice1", … in the order the caller declared them, the LAST being the safe/negative default that Esc and the title-bar X resolve to. They used to set no Name at all and were addressable only by `name` (the Danish button text). DialogNotFound when no modal is open; zero controls on a resolved modal is a WALK FAILURE, not a fact about the dialog -- capture.modal before recording it.
commands.note: The counterpart to the vendor's dialog.read, and deliberately the same shape so compare3 C1.2c can compare the two variable dialogs. It SUPPLIES the readback the four dialog-opening rows lack (node.getProperties, node.rename, projectInfo.get, modules.list) -- but it does not change what those rows do: each still opens its dialog and stops, so they stay partial and the readback is THIS command, run next. (Corrected 2026-08-02: the note used to say it 'unblocks' them, which read as though their status had changed.)

commands.description: Type a value into a field of the OPEN modal: --field <AutomationId|Name> --text <value> (also positional: `dialog set-text NameBox "New name"`). The write counterpart to dialog.read, so an "edit via its properties dialog" flow can go past the inventory. Fields address by AutomationId (Avalonia falls back to x:Name, so NameBox/NoteBox work) and then by UIA Name. Sets through ValuePattern, NOT keystrokes: a keystroke needs the foreground, goes wherever focus is, and APPENDS to what the field already holds, whereas SetValue replaces it. The value is read back and returned as data.readBack -- a read-only or one-way-bound field accepts the call and keeps its old text, which comes back as Code=NoEffect rather than a false success. Open the dialog first (node.getProperties) and commit it with dialog.click --button OK.
commands.note: Added 2026-08-01 (uxparity S-08) for the DLG scenarios that must SET fields, not just read them: S-08, S-13, S-14, S-19, S-32.

commands.description: Choose an item in a DROP-DOWN of the open modal: --field <AutomationId|Name> and --text <item> or --index <n> (also positional: `dialog select-item DataLineList 1`). Text matches EXACTLY first, then a UNIQUE case-insensitive contains; an ambiguous match is refused with TargetAmbiguous rather than resolved to the first hit. Needed because dialog.setText answers 'not a text field' on a ComboBox and dialog.click resolves buttons -- the second dialog control type that was undrivable from this side after check boxes (alignment F-37), while the vendor driver has had dialog.selectItem all along. EXPANDS the drop-down before enumerating, deliberately: Avalonia realizes a ComboBox's items lazily, so one whose list has never been opened reports ZERO items -- which is also why dialog.read shows items:[] for it. The list is collapsed again afterwards. Verified by reading the SELECTION back, so data.selectedAfter records what actually happened; data.items[] carries the realized list, which is the only way to enumerate a drop-down on this side.
commands.note: Added 2026-08-11 while verifying alignment F-33's address lists, which could be read but not driven. PROMOTED to confirmed the same day by reading the effect back from the running app: on the terminal address editor it selected data line '1' (17 items realized: 'ikke konfigureret' plus 1-16), which enabled the terminal list, then terminal '3' (8 items), after which OK armed and committing reported 'Udgang blev adresseret til datalinie 1, klemme 3.' NOTE the read-back is by TEXT: a collapsed Avalonia ComboBox virtualizes its items away, so GetSelection() is empty and dialog.read reports items:[] and selectedIndex:-1 for it -- the control's `text` is the field that carries the selection once the list is closed.

commands.description: ACTIVATE A ROW (or one CELL of a row) inside the open modal with real mouse input: --field <list AutomationId|Name>, then --row <n> (0-based) or --text <row text>, optionally --column <header|AutomationId|cell text|index> and --double. This is the gesture the parity checklist's interaction dimension asks for -- 'is this row clickable, and what does activating it open?' -- and the one thing this driver could not do: dialog.click drives NAMED BUTTONS, node.doubleClick drives TREE rows, and neither reaches a row inside a dialog's grid, so every such question was answered from a screenshot (presentation only) instead of exercised. GENERAL by construction: any list-like container in any dialog, no knowledge of module maps, terminals or scenes. A CELL is addressed as a refinement of its row rather than by a second verb, because clicking a cell and clicking a row are the same gesture at different coordinates -- which matters wherever the vendor makes individual COLUMNS editable. Effect-verified like the vendor's verb: Ok only if the selection actually lands on the requested row or a dialog is raised, else NoEffect; data.openedDialog names anything the gesture opened, data.hitArea records whether the row or a column was struck. Refuses to click a row with no on-screen rectangle rather than clicking blind, and says so when a virtualized list has realized no rows.
commands.note: Added 2026-08-11. Mirrors the vendor MCP's dialog_clickRow (controlId + 0-based row + doubleClick) so both sides' transcripts compare like for like; addressing differs because Avalonia has no numeric control ids. --column has no vendor counterpart yet: the vendor verb clicks the row only, so per-column comparisons still need that side extended. Status partial until exercised live against an editable grid.

commands.description: Tick or untick a CHECK BOX in the open modal: --field <AutomationId|Name> [--on|--off] (also positional: `dialog set-check SaveOnPowerLossBox --off`). Ticking is the default. Needed because dialog.click resolves BUTTONS only, so a dialog checkbox was undrivable from this side while the vendor driver has had dialog.setCheck all along -- an asymmetry that left every dialog checkbox unverifiable live (alignment F-31). IDEMPOTENT: TogglePattern.Toggle() flips, so the current state is read first and the toggle sent only when it differs; asking for a state the box is already in is an Ok no-op, not a flip away from it. Verified by reading ToggleState BACK, so data.before/after/toggled record what actually happened rather than what was asked for.
commands.note: Added 2026-08-11 for alignment F-27's power-fail checkbox, which until then had to be driven from the context flyout instead. PROMOTED to confirmed the same day by reading the effect back from the running app: on a Flag's properties dialog it took the box Off->On (toggled:true, verified), reported toggled:false when asked for On again, committed with the status line 'Vaerdien gemmes ved stroemsvigt.', read back On after reopening the dialog, and --off reversed it and persisted that too.

commands.description: Invoke a named button in the open modal: --button "No"|"Yes"|"OK"|"Cancel". Needed because not every dialog honours Esc (OpenVisual's Delete confirm does not), and an undismissable modal blocks every later command. OpenVisual dialogs are SEPARATE TOP-LEVEL WINDOWS (Views\ResultDialog.cs calls ShowDialog(owner); the app defines 14 dialog Window subclasses beside MainWindow); this resolves the modal with Get-OpenModalWindow -- a RootElement search for a ControlType.Window in the app's process that is not the main window BY WINDOW HANDLE (it used to be 'whose title is not the main window's', which hid the About dialog, titled 'About IHC OpenVisual') -- and then searches THAT window's subtree. On an unknown --button it lists the buttons it did find. dialog.cancel falls back to No/Cancel/Annuller/Nej/Close/Luk automatically -- dismissal labels only, never OK/Yes, since a "cancel" that commits is worse than one that fails.
commands.note: CORRECTED 2026-07-17 (enabler3 S3): this row previously asserted OpenVisual's dialogs are 'IN-WINDOW OVERLAYS - one HWND, buttons are descendants of the main window'. That was wrong, and two independent sources agree it was: the app shows every dialog via ResultDialog<TResult> -> ShowDialog(owner) across separate Windows, and this driver's OWN Get-OpenModalWindow has always found them by searching RootElement for a separate top-level Window. The overlay claim never matched the code that was already working underneath it.

commands.description: List every semantic command with status (machine-readable self-description).

List insertable products by walking Insert > Products > … into data.titles[]. Raise --depth (default 2) to descend into product categories; the paths it reports are what product.insert --menu-path consumes.

List FB templates by walking Indsæt > FunktionsBlokke > … into data.titles[]. Raise --depth (default 2) to descend; the paths it reports are what fb.insertTemplate --menu-path consumes. Repointed 2026-08-04 from Bibliotek, which used to carry a second copy of the same submenu; the vendor has it under Indsæt only.
Capture the whole app window to a PNG (foregrounds it first).
Capture the client area to a PNG.
commands.note: Currently captures the full window frame (Avalonia chrome is minimal); true client-rect trim not yet split out.

commands.description: Capture the open modal dialog to a PNG; DialogNotFound if none is open.
Capture the child control addressed by --id <AutomationId> to a PNG.
New project (toolbar New). If there are unsaved changes a save-guard dialog appears — answer it with dialog.cancel or save first.

Open a project file: raises the toolbar Open picker, types --path <file> into it and commits. Verifies by effect (the title bar must name the file) and reports which check carried it in data.verifiedBy. That check is 'titleBaseName': an exact literal prefix comparison, NOT a wildcard match ('[' and ']' are legal in a Windows filename and would be read as a character class). The caption carries no directory, so it cannot tell this file from another of the same name in another folder -- the leftover-modal check (DialogBlocked) is what catches the usual form of that trap. If the current project has unsaved changes a save-guard may appear first — deal with it before calling this.
Save project (toolbar Save). An untitled project raises Save-As instead.

Save the project to --path <file> via Filer > Gem projekt som…: types the path into the save picker and commits, verifying by effect. A ROOTED --path is verified against the filesystem (data.verifiedBy 'fileOnDisk'), which the title bar cannot do -- it carries the base name only, so it cannot tell 'written where I asked' from 'a file of that name was already open'; a relative path falls back to the caption ('titleBaseName') because the picker resolves it against ITS working directory, not this session's. Refuses an existing target unless --overwrite is passed, which also answers the picker's replace prompt.
List recent projects by walking Filer > Seneste projekter. Read data.titles[0] and find the 'Seneste projekter' child; its children are the MRU entries in menu order.

Return to configuration view / leave programming mode (Esc). GLOBAL, so it takes no --path. Effect-verified 2026-07-16: both pane roots return from the FB's name to 'Lokaliteter' -- read it with `tree dump --depth 1`, which since enabler3 really does bound the walk to the root (it was silently ignored before, so this documented one-node probe used to realize the entire pane).

Enter programming mode for a function block (F3): pass --path (and --tree TV2) to address it, or select an FB first, else it is a no-op. READ THE EFFECT with `tree dump --depth 1` on EITHER pane: in configuration mode both panes root at 'Lokaliteter'; in programming mode BOTH re-root at the FB's own name (its Input/Output sections beneath). Since enabler3 `--depth 1` really does bound the walk to the root -- it was silently swallowed before, so this probe used to realize the entire pane on every call. context.statusText also says 'Programmeringstilstand -- tryk Esc for at vende tilbage til konfiguration.' Effect-verified 2026-07-16 -- this closes census E-3, which recorded the transition as unmeasurable; the same pane-root probe reads the vendor too (whose tree.read --depth is likewise real). READ THE EFFECT YOURSELF: like every `key` row, this one returns Ok with verified:false and never probes the roots. (The vendor driver returns NoEffect when the roots do not move; an earlier version of this sentence carried that clause where it read as a promise about THIS command -- corrected 2026-08-02.)

Enumerate the toolbar in BAR ORDER into data.buttons[] as {index, id, name, enabled, separator, rect} -- the same shape the vendor driver's `toolbar.dump` emits, so the two bars diff mechanically. Separators are rows of their own (separator:true), because GROUPING is part of what a bar says and a run of buttons with a rule between them is not the same bar as one without. Read-only: it opens nothing and invokes nothing. Returns ControlNotFound while the toolbar is hidden (Vis > Vaerktoejslinie) -- that is a real state, not a fault.
commands.note: Added 2026-08-11 to close alignment F-7, the OpenVisual half of the toolbar-reader gap the vendor side closed in turn 2. It depends on OpenVisual publishing its separators: they were Rectangles, which no automation client can see, so this dump would have reported a bar with no grouping at all (alignment F-45, fixed in the same turn). Status partial until a second bar state is read -- so far it has only been run against the default bar.

commands.description: Toggle toolbar visibility (Vis > Værktøjslinie).
Toggle status bar visibility (Vis > Statuslinie). Invoke as `view statusbar-toggle`.

Show or hide the Problemer panel (Vis > Problemer). Invoke as `view problems-toggle`. It belongs to the view family, beside toolbar and statusbar, because it is a MENU row -- the problems.* verbs drive the panel's own controls. The path pins the menu item's AutomationId rather than its Danish label, per this file's note; the two sibling rows still pin labels and are left alone.

Read the Problemer panel: visibility, the four-state readiness (validating|clean|findings|stale), the state line's Danish text, whether a result is BOUND, whether the staleness indicator is engaged, the three live per-severity counts and how many rows are realized. Pass --wait to poll until a result is bound (--timeout ms, default 15000). WAIT BEFORE YOU ASSERT: the panel validates in the background, so for at least the 300ms debounce plus one whole-project run after a launch or an open it reports state=validating and NO counts are meaningful yet. A read taken before that is not wrong, it is early.

List the realized rows of the Problemer panel: index, code (the row's AutomationId), occurrence (the row's ItemStatus -- its per-occurrence identity), severity, message, element and bounding rect. Address a row by `occurrence`, not by `code`: several codes fire many times over one project, so a code names a whole group and only the occurrence identity names ONE row. The list VIRTUALIZES, so this reports what is realized rather than every finding -- read the counts from problems.state for the totals. Severity/message/element are split from the row's accessible name, which the app composes as '<Alvor>: <Besked> (<Element>)'.

Click a Problemer row with real pointer input: --row <index|occurrence|code|text>, optionally --double. A single click ONLY SELECTS the row -- no tree moves, no mode changes, nothing opens; --double ACTIVATES, which reveals the row's element in the owning tree pane (entering or leaving programming mode if the target needs it) and follows the row's full route on to the dialog and field the fix is made in. The two are different gestures and mean different things here, so pass --double whenever you are asserting about navigation. The selectors are tried most-specific first: the per-occurrence identity from problems.rows (unique), then the code (which several rows share by design, so it reaches whichever comes past first), then a fragment of the row's accessible sentence. A row that names no element changes nothing under either gesture. REAL POINTER, not a selection call: setting the selection directly would reach the outcome by a path no user can take. Verify the effect with tree.selection, not from this verb's own envelope.

Flip one severity filter: --tier <error|warning|info>. Driven through the UIA Toggle pattern, the same door a keyboard or screen-reader user uses. Hiding a tier hides its ROWS ONLY -- its count, and the send gate, are unmoved, because hiding a finding is not fixing it. Reports before/after toggle state and how many rows remain shown.

Sort the Problemer list by a column: --column <severity|code|message|element|category>. Invokes that column's header button, so a second call on the same column reverses the direction (two directions only -- there is no third state). Reports the row codes before and after plus whether the order actually moved.

Set the workspace text size (Vis > Tekststørrelse). Pass --menu-path with the step label -- "Lille", "Normal", "Stor" or "Størst". Scales every workspace font token at once; US-001. Session-scoped, so it does not survive a restart.

Select a node (single click) by label path ("Localities/Kitchen") or 0-based index path ("0") in --tree TV1 (installation, default) or TV2 (functions). Verifies the caret landed. Prerequisite for selection-relative commands.
Single-click select a node by --path (alias of tree.select).
Expand a tree node via the ExpandCollapse pattern. Select by --path (and --tree).
Collapse a tree node via the ExpandCollapse pattern. Select by --path (and --tree).

Double-click (activate) a node. Select by --path (and --tree); the row is scrolled into view for you. Clicks the node's OWN header strip and hit-tests that point back to the target before clicking, reporting data.targetVerified:true -- an Avalonia TreeViewItem's bounds enclose its whole EXPANDED SUBTREE, so a naive rect-centre/GetClickablePoint() click silently lands on a DESCENDANT row and still reports success (this fabricated census cells: 'double-click does nothing on a locality' when the locality was never clicked). If no point on the row hit-tests back to it (occluded, or clipped by the tree's own scrollbar) it returns TargetNotFound rather than clicking a different row. --x-offset N clicks N px RIGHT OF THE ROW'S LABEL instead of on it -- census C16 (does a double-click in the empty space past a short label still activate the row?); the same hit-test-back guard applies, so an offset that leaves the row/viewport is REFUSED rather than clamped, and data.hitArea echoes which point ran. EFFECT (re-read from the app 2026-08-02): double-click is HANDLED -- MainWindow.axaml binds DoubleTapped on the row content and MainWindow.axaml.cs selects the row, runs ActivateNodeCommand and marks the event Handled, so it OPENS THE NODE'S PROPERTIES DIALOG and the Avalonia default expand-toggle does NOT run. A pin opens its owning product's dialog; the Localities root, link rows and unresolvable rows do nothing. Read the result with session.status.openModal / dialog.read and close it with dialog.click or dialog.cancel. (This row previously said no node type handled double-click and that expandable nodes would toggle -- both halves went stale when the activation handler landed.) COORDINATE NOTE: data.point is a diagnostic for a mis-aimed gesture -- it records where the driver actually clicked, so a wrong landing stays readable after the fact -- and NOT an input: do not hand it to SetCursorPos or do coordinate math on it. Address the node with --path (and --tree) instead; every pointing command here is path-addressed, so no caller needs a screen coordinate. That the point is declared (native space plus the sibling in the other one, see doctor's display block) is what makes a mis-aimed gesture diagnosable, not an invitation to re-use the number: a coordinate carried into another process is the failure this note exists to prevent.
commands.note: C16 TRAP, measured 2026-07-17 (enabler3 S5): on THIS side the DEFAULT click point is already in the empty space right of a short label. Get-TreeItemClickPoint takes the ROW rect's centre, and the row rect spans the pane width -- clicking 'Stue' landed at x=728 while the label ends near x=301, so the default and the --x-offset 40 point (x=341) are BOTH right of the text, just at different distances. The vendor is not like this: its click point comes from TVM_GETITEMRECT(wParam=TRUE), the LABEL-only rect (measured: label right=106, row right=641, so a 535 px gap). So a C16 comparison of 'default double-click' against 'default double-click' is NOT comparing the same hit area -- pin both sides with an explicit --x-offset, or the cell measures the two drivers' click-point conventions rather than the two apps.

commands.description: Right-click a node with the REAL mouse and report what it did to the selection: data.selectedBefore/selectedAfter/selectionMoved answer 'does right-click move the caret?' (C2/D3), and data.items[] carries whatever flyout it raised. Deliberately does NOT select the target first -- selecting it would answer the question in advance -- so point --path at a node that is NOT currently selected and a no-op stays distinguishable from a hit. Distinct from menu.dumpContext, whose Shift+F10 is a KEYBOARD gesture acting on the already-focused row and so cannot move the caret by construction. COORDINATE NOTE: data.point is a diagnostic for a mis-aimed gesture -- it records where the driver actually clicked, so a wrong landing stays readable after the fact -- and NOT an input: do not hand it to SetCursorPos or do coordinate math on it. Address the node with --path (and --tree) instead; every pointing command here is path-addressed, so no caller needs a screen coordinate. That the point is declared (native space plus the sibling in the other one, see doctor's display block) is what makes a mis-aimed gesture diagnosable, not an invitation to re-use the number: a coordinate carried into another process is the failure this note exists to prevent.
commands.note: Effect-verified 2026-07-16 (verify2) against a same-integrity elevated app: with 'Stue' selected, right-clicking 'Udestue' reported selectedBefore=Stue, selectedAfter=Udestue, selectionMoved=true, flyoutOpened=true, 7 items -- so right-click DOES move the caret, and the readback proves it hit the addressed node.

commands.description: Read a node's tooltip (exposed to automation as HelpText). Address it with --path (and --tree). The row is RESOLVED, not selected: since 2026-08-02 this reader no longer moves the caret (it used to, silently, which pre-answers the very question node.rightClick measures). mutating is noState rather than no only because reaching a deep row still expands its ancestors.

Recursively dump a pane's tree as JSON {pane, capturedAfter, expandAll, withKind, maxDepth, nodeCount, root:{label, expanded, children[]}} in data. --tree TV1|TV2, optional --path to scope to a subtree, --after <slug> to stamp capturedAfter. --path RESOLVES the subtree without selecting it (since 2026-08-02 -- it used to select, so dumping a subtree to choose a target moved the caret you were about to measure); mutating is noState rather than no because reaching a deep row expands its ancestors. --depth/--after are read as NAMED flags only, so a positional path cannot be swallowed by either. Does NOT expand collapsed nodes (expansion state is itself observable data) unless --expand-all is passed; collapsed nodes report expanded:false with children:[] because Avalonia does not realize their children. --depth N bounds the walk (default 40) -- use --depth 1 for the mode probe, which reads the root only instead of realizing the whole pane. --with-kind adds `kind` per node (the row's TYPE, from AutomationId): needed in programming mode, where the LABEL is user data and cannot identify a row -- 'Kip Udgang' is a command, 'Kip ved kort tryk -> ON' an event. Additive and off by default so the schema stays identical to the vendor's tree.read dump and tools\tree-diff.ps1 keeps working. Children come from the control-view TreeWalker, the same enumeration --path resolution uses: FindAll(TreeScope::Children) does not return a TreeViewItem's own rows in this app (it skips real children and runs past the end of the subtree), and this dump -- the comparison's structural oracle -- used it while reporting verified:true until 2026-08-02.

Send a raw key gesture in SendKeys syntax to the app: --gesture "{F2}"|"{DOWN}"|"+{F10}"|"{DELETE}"|"{ESC}". Optional --path (+--tree) selects a node first so the key lands on a known selection. data reports the selection/modal/title before and after so the effect is readable from the envelope. Refuses {F5} (controller Send-project), and requires --confirm-destructive for {DELETE}/{DEL}: MainWindow routes Key.Delete to the edit.delete command, so the raw gesture IS node.delete, and this row's gates:[] would otherwise be a way around the removal gate. Answering the confirmation prompt it raises stays ungated (dialog.click).
commands.note: GATED 2026-08-02. Also fixed here: --path is optional, but the returned delta read the tree id unconditionally, so the plain form threw under StrictMode AFTER SendWait had fired -- the gesture happened and the envelope said MutationFailed, inviting a retry that would repeat it.

commands.description: Open the context flyout on the current selection (Shift+F10), enumerate its items with enabled state into data.items[], screenshot it, then close it. --depth N (default 1, matching the vendor driver's context default) bounds submenu recursion: depth 1 is the flat top level, 2 lists each submenu's leaves in children[] -- raise it whenever a row offers a nested palette (a section's 'Insert variable >'), because a flat read reports that whole palette as ONE item while the vendor lists its leaves. Rows carry the same {label, accelerator, separator, enabled, children[]} shape as menu.dumpBar. The screenshot is taken BEFORE descending, so it always shows the top level. Select the node with --path (and --tree) first. noState, not no: unlike the other readers this one MUST select and focus the addressed row, because Shift+F10 acts on whatever holds keyboard focus -- so it does move the caret. Fails TargetNotFound if the flyout does not open, and NEVER returns an empty inventory as a verified reading: both trees share one MenuFlyout resource, so zero items always means the gesture failed, never 'this node type has no menu'. data.attempts reports whether the bounded retry was needed -- a recurring 2 means the foreground/focus order regressed.

Walk the menu bar and enumerate titles/items/enabled state into data.titles[] (nested children[]) -- the same {titleCount, maxDepth, titles:[{label, enabled, children[]}]} shape the vendor driver's `app menu dump-bar` emits, so the two sides' submenu trees diff mechanically. --menu <Title> narrows to one title; --depth N (default 2, matching the vendor's default) bounds submenu recursion -- raise it to reach catalog leaves, which nest 4+ deep, and heed the truncation warning. --with-id appends each row's AutomationId (the app's CommandRegistry row id, e.g. "file.new"); ADDITIVE and off by default so the default shape stays identical to the vendor's and mechanical diffs keep working -- the same discipline as tree.dump's --with-kind. Opens and closes real menus by HOVER, never clicking a leaf, so it is slow but it cannot invoke anything by accident.
commands.note: CORRECTED 2026-08-08: this row justified the hover walk with "it is the only route: Avalonia menu items expose no UIA patterns". That WAS true -- Avalonia 12.1.1's MenuItemAutomationPeer implements IToggleProvider and nothing else -- but OpenVisual now supplies AccessibleMenu/AccessibleMenuItem, whose peer adds Invoke and ExpandCollapse, so menu items DO carry patterns here (verified live: every bar title reports ExpandCollapse, every leaf Invoke). menu.invoke and the `menu` mechanism now use them. This DUMP keeps hovering on purpose: hover realizes a submenu without any chance of activating a leaf, which is the property an enumerator needs.

commands.description: Invoke a menu-bar command BY AutomationId, with no path to spell: --id <AutomationId>, e.g. `aui menu invoke --id file.saveAs`. The ids ARE the app's CommandRegistry row ids (file.new, edit.cut, view.showProgram, reports.functions, project.info); top-level titles are MenuFile/MenuEdit/…; items with no registry row take menu.* / theme.* / textScale.*. Prefer this over --menu-path: a path is a list of Danish labels carrying access-key underscores and a real ellipsis character ("Gem projekt _som…"), which is exactly the literal that goes stale silently -- report.generate shipped for months with a menuPath whose every segment was wrong. The id says nothing about WHERE the item lives, so this opens each top-level menu in turn and searches it, expanding containers and invoking nothing until the id matches; a menu that does not hold it is closed again. Enumerate the available ids with `menu dump-bar --with-id --depth 3`. Verified:false by design -- activation is not the same as the intended effect, so read the effect back yourself. Returns data.menuPath so the run records WHERE the id was found.
commands.note: Added 2026-08-08, enabled by the app's AccessibleMenuItem peer (Invoke + ExpandCollapse). Before that no menu item exposed a UIA pattern and the only route was a synthesized click at a screen coordinate.

commands.description:
Insert a catalog product into the selected locality. Select the locality with tree.select first, then address the catalog subtree with --menu-path, e.g. --menu-path "Datalinie produkter/<category>/<product>". Use `aui catalog products` to discover the available paths.

THIS VERB STOPS AT A DIALOG, ALWAYS, AND DELIBERATELY. Placing a product raises that product's properties dialog -- since 2026-08-12 ONE window serves every family, automation id `ProductDialogWindow`, titled with the product TYPE (a modem's is "SMS Modem Egenskaber"): the per-family ModemPropertiesWindow/ProductPropertiesWindow are gone, so do not key on them. The insert is not settled until the dialog is answered: `dialog click --button OK` commits it, `dialog click --button Annuller` rolls it back so nothing is added. So this command is the FIRST STEP of a sequence -- follow it with session.status (or dialog.read) and then a dialog.* verb, exactly like node.getProperties. It does not answer or dismiss the dialog for you, and it must not be changed to: a verb that swallows the dialog would report an insert as though no dialog existed, which is the exact mis-measurement that produced a round trip in the app (see the routeNote).

Note what the tree does WHILE that dialog is up: IHC OpenVisual has already added the row, and rolls it back on cancel; the reference application adds nothing until OK. That is a registered deliberate difference (product.md, alignment F-14), not a defect -- do not raise it as a finding.
commands.note: Menu walk, dialog and rollback all verified live 2026-08-11 against the running app, on an untitled template project with 'Stue' selected: `product insert --menu-path "Bus Produkter/SMS Modem"` returned Ok having invoked 'Indsæt/Produkter/Bus Produkter/SMS Modem'; session.status then reported openModal {title: 'SMS Modem Egenskaber', id: 'ModemPropertiesWindow'} and the tree had ALREADY grown 11 -> 12 nodes -- NOTE, that id is HISTORICAL: the per-family windows were replaced by the one generic 'ProductDialogWindow' on 2026-08-12 (the title is unchanged), so expect that id today (Stue gained one child) while the modal was up; `dialog click --button Annuller` returned Ok and the tree went back to 11 with Stue at 0 children and the status line 'Indsætning af \'SMS Modem\' annulleret.'. Promoted partial -> confirmed on that read-back. The per-product leaf paths still depend on the loaded catalog, so an unknown --menu-path is a catalog question, not a wiring one. Runs WITHOUT the foreground: the menu mechanism walks via the ExpandCollapse/Invoke patterns, so no input is synthesized (dialog.cancel by contrast sends Esc and does need it -- use dialog.click --button, which invokes the button's pattern).

commands.description: Invoke a context-flyout item on the addressed row: --path <row> [--tree] --item <AutomationId|label>. Ids are matched FIRST and are the app's CommandRegistry row ids under a 'ctx.' prefix (ctx.edit.cut, ctx.node.properties, ctx.program.addProgram) -- prefer them, since a Danish label with an access-key underscore is the literal that goes stale. Enumerate both with `menu dump-context --with-id`. A '/' walks one submenu level ('Insert variable/Input'); escape a literal slash as '\/'. This is the generic form of the pinned-item rows (fb.unlock, node.delete, …) and exists so a census can exercise authoring items -- Logic group, Sub-program, Add Powerup event, Use in program -- without a registry row per item. Enumerate first with menu.dumpContext: a missing item returns TargetNotFound listing what WAS realized, and a present-but-greyed one returns PreconditionMissing rather than a hopeful Ok. Verified:false by design -- the flyout closing proves the item ACTIVATED, not that it had its intended effect, so read the effect back yourself.

commands.description: Undo the last change (Ctrl+Z). GLOBAL, so it takes no --path: it acts on the document, not the selection. Effect-verified 2026-07-16 by tree delta (it reverted a cross-locality move: source 4->5, target 5->4).

Move a node onto another by a REAL mouse drag: --from <path> --to <path> [--from-tree TV1|TV2] [--to-tree TV1|TV2]. Legacy --tree selects both endpoints for same-pane calls. The gesture the menu supplements (edit.moveUp/moveDown, link start-from-here/to-here) stand in for, so a 3WAY scenario can prove supplement and drag agree -- without it the OpenVisual drag path itself is never measured. Synthesized as press, threshold nudge, interpolated moves, release: a drag only STARTS once the pointer travels past the toolkit's drag threshold while held, and it drops where the pointer last moved, so a single jump between down and up is delivered as a plain CLICK on the source row. Steals the foreground for the whole gesture and refuses rather than dragging blind. Same-pane effects require a changed row order. Cross-pane program-authoring effects require a changed status that names both addressed endpoints; cross-pane link effects require both endpoint child counts to increase. Code=NoEffect when the applicable oracle sees nothing.
commands.note: Added 2026-08-01 (uxparity S-11). Counterpart to the vendor driver's node.drag.

Open the About dialog (toolbar Help/About). It is a separate top-level window -- titled "Om IHC OpenVisual" (the UI is Danish) and carrying AutomationId "AboutWindow" -- so it BLOCKS every later command until dismissed: read it with dialog.read, close it with dialog.cancel (or dialog.click --button CloseButton). Prefer context.openModal.id over its title when branching on which dialog is up.
commands.note: Until 2026-08-02 this dialog was invisible to the whole dialog surface: Get-OpenModalWindow identified the main window by title suffix, and this caption ends with the product name, so context.openModal read null, dialog.read/capture.modal answered DialogNotFound, and dialog.cancel returned ok:true 'No modal open.' while it sat there blocking the queue. The modal is now identified by window HANDLE, so About behaves like any other dialog.
